The lunar month is divided into two Pakshas (fortnights). Shukla Paksha is the waxing phase (growing Moon), and Krishna Paksha is the waning phase (receding Moon).
Pratipada (Joyful): The beginning of the lunar phase. Ideal for new beginnings, religious ceremonies, and sowing seeds.
Dwitiya (Lucky): A day of growth and stability. Auspicious for laying foundations, weddings, and permanent works.
Tritiya (Victorious): Excellent for music, arts, and moving into a new home. Akshaya Tritiya falls on this day.
Chaturthi (Empty): Sacred to Lord Ganesha. While generally avoided for business, it is powerful for overcoming obstacles and spiritual work.
Panchami (Full): A day of wisdom and healing. Favorable for medicine, study, and attaining knowledge.
Shasthi (Joyful): Sacred to Lord Kartikeya. Good for building power, festivities, and strengthening friendships.
Saptami (Lucky): Sacred to the Sun God. Ideal for starting journeys, health regimens, and buying vehicles.
Ashtami (Victorious): Sacred to Goddess Durga and Lord Krishna. A day for courage and strength, though travel is usually avoided.
Navami (Empty): Sacred to Lord Rama. While inauspicious for new worldly tasks, it is powerful for destroying negative habits.
Dashami (Full): Highly auspicious for virtuous acts, duty (Dharma), and spiritual growth.
Ekadashi (Joyful): The most sacred day for fasting and devotion to Lord Vishnu. Brings purification of mind and body.
Dwadashi (Lucky): A day of fulfillment and completion of rituals. Symbolizes the light of the 12 Adityas.
Trayodashi (Victorious): Sacred to Lord Shiva (Pradosham). Excellent for forming connections, romance, and spiritual joy.
Chaturdashi (Empty): Sacred to Lord Shiva (Shivaratri). A day of high energy, best suited for meditation and internal transformation.
Purnima (Full): Full Moon day. Auspicious for growth, celebrations, and seeking blessings for prosperity.
Amavasya (Full): New Moon day. A day for introspection, spiritual silence, and honoring ancestors (Pitrus).
Ashwini: Healing. \"Physician of the Gods.\" Ideal for starting medical treatments and quick actions.
Bharani: Transformation. Represents the cycle of life and rebirth. A day for discipline and creativity.
Krittika: Purification. \"The Star of Fire.\" Sharp intellect; ideal for burning away negativity and bad habits.
Rohini: Growth. \"The Chariot.\" Star of abundance and beauty. Excellent for business and farming.
Mrigashira: Search. Represents the soul\'s quest for truth. Good for research, travel, and curiosity.
Ardra: Breakthrough. Transformation through emotion. A day to wash away the old and start fresh.
Punarvasu: Resilience. \"The Return of Light.\" Signifies hope and success on the second attempt.
Pushya: Nourishment. The most auspicious star for spiritual growth. Ideal for gurus and teaching.
Ashlesha: Intuition. Star of deep insight and strategy. Good for planning and inward reflection.
Magha: Heritage. \"The Royal Throne.\" Connects to ancestors. Best for honoring lineage and duty.
Purva Phalguni: Relaxation. Star of joy and luxury. Excellent for social events and the arts.
Uttara Phalguni: Duty. Signifies service and stable relationships. Good for contracts and help.
Hasta: Skill. \"The Hand.\" Power to manifest. Ideal for crafts, business, and skill-based work.
Chitra: Creativity. \"The Jewel.\" Focuses on beauty and structure. Good for design and aesthetics.
Swati: Independence. Represents freedom and the intellect. Best for communication and diplomacy.
Vishakha: Purpose. Single-minded determination to reach goals. Good for focus and ambition.
Anuradha: Devotion. \"The Lotus.\" Thriving in challenges. Excellent for loyalty and friendship.
Jyeshtha: Authority. Signifies seniority and responsibility. Good for leadership and protection.
Mula: Truth. \"The Roots.\" Getting to the core of reality. Best for deep research and silence.
Purva Ashadha: Invincibility. Purifying power. Good for cleansing and filtration of ideas.
Uttara Ashadha: Righteousness. \"The Tusk.\" Permanent success through discipline and Dharma.
Shravana: Listening. \"The Ear.\" Star of learning and oral traditions. Ideal for study and silence.
Dhanishta: Harmony. Rhythm of the universe. Good for music, wealth, and group activities.
Shatabhisha: Mystery. \"The Hundred Physicians.\" Star of hidden healing and solve mysteries.
Purva Bhadrapada: Penance. Transformative fire. Ideal for deep meditation and spiritual breakthroughs.
Uttara Bhadrapada: Wisdom. \"Serpent of the Deep.\" Grounded wisdom and control over emotions.
Revati: Liberation. Safe journey back to the source. Star of compassion and safe travel.
Tithi is the lunar day. Each Tithi has specific energy influencing daily activities.
Pratipada: Good for religious ceremonies and starting new ventures.
Dwitiya: Auspicious for laying foundations, weddings, and long-term investments.
Tritiya: Very auspicious for all virtuous deeds and auspicious beginnings.
Chaturthi: Associated with Lord Ganesha. Good for removing obstacles, but generally avoided for weddings.
Panchami: Favorable for all religious activities and administrative work.
Shashti: Associated with Lord Muruga. Favorable for construction and courageous deeds.
Saptami: Auspicious for starting journeys and medical treatments.
Ashtami: Suitable for finishing tasks, but avoid starting new ventures if possible.
Navami: Generally avoided for auspicious beginnings; good for conquering enemies or legal matters.
Dashami: Highly auspicious for all kinds of work, travels, and new ventures.
Ekadashi: Excellent for fasting, spiritual practices, and religious observances.
Dwadashi: Good for charity and completing religious rituals started on Ekadashi.
Trayodashi: Associated with Pradosham. Good for friendship, arts, and spiritual growth.
Chaturdashi: Avoid for auspicious beginnings; suitable for spiritual practices and finishing tasks.
Pournami: Extremely auspicious for all virtuous deeds, meditation, and rituals.
Amavasai: Dedicated to ancestors (Pitrus). Good for charity and spiritual introspection; avoid new ventures.
The Nakshatra or Star during this period influences the mental and emotional state. This star is traditionally used to determine suitability for activities.
Krittika: Associated with fire. Good for purification, hard work, and technical tasks.
Rohini: Very auspicious. Ideal for growth, creativity, and all positive beginnings.
Pushya: The most auspicious star for all virtuous and nourishing activities.
An auspicious period dedicated to Lord Shiva. Ideal for seeking forgiveness and spiritual liberation.
A monthly observance for Lord Shiva. Focus on meditation, fasting, and spiritual vigil.
Aadi Kiruthigai: A significant festival dedicated to Lord Muruga, occurring during the month of Aadi on the Krittika Nakshatra. It is a day for intense devotion and seeking divine protection.
Aadi Pooram: A special day celebrating the birth of Andal, an incarnation of Goddess Lakshmi. It is observed with great fervor in temples across Tamil Nadu.
A special religious or traditional event observed during this period.
The Tamil Calendar is a sidereal solar calendar used traditionally in Tamil Nadu. It marks months based on the sun\'s entry into zodiac signs.
This month in the Tamil calendar has unique spiritual and seasonal significance.
The "Time of Brahma." Highly auspicious for meditation, yoga, and starting the day with focus.
The most auspicious time of the day for any work. Success is highly likely.
A verified auspicious window for significant life events.
